note: THE SECTION LIST, AND THE ORDER OF IT. Created 2026-08-20 (Prompt E item 5). A section is identified by its SLUG, never by a number: rows carry the slug, and display order is this array's order. Inserting a new state's hunt section is one line added here, and it renumbers nothing, because there are no numbers to renumber. Sections are by AREA OF THE PROJECT, not by dependency — dependency information stays on each row and orders rows inside a section. RULING 32: there is no holding section and no miscellaneous bucket. A row that fits nowhere is evidence this list is incomplete, and the answer is a named section proposed in a session report.

sections.title: Needs Sean
sections.what: Anything only Sean can unblock: an API key, a legal review, a business decision, a visual judgment, and specifically go look at the site and confirm this is right.

priorities.P1: The product is broken or fundamentally different. It doesn't open, or something is drastically changed from what shipped before. Look now.
priorities.P2: New information landed, confirm it reads right. A named body or class, and a sample size.
priorities.P3: A small adjustment. Tell me if you like it.

sections.title: New Hampshire hunt
sections.what: Everything owed to a reader in New Hampshire — Newbury and 03255 first. Bodies, officeholders, candidates, meetings, the ballot.

sections.title: New Jersey hunt
sections.what: Everything owed to a reader in New Jersey — Rockaway Township and 07866 first.

sections.title: Arizona hunt
sections.what: Everything owed to a reader in Arizona — Vail (85641) and downtown Tucson (85701) first.

sections.title: Visual feedback
sections.what: Everything arriving in Sean's twice-weekly batches — what the product looks like and reads like when he walks it.

sections.title: Data infrastructure
sections.what: Sources, ingest, denominators, extraction, crawlers. The machinery that turns a public record into a row.

sections.title: Product / UI
sections.what: How the app behaves and reads — surfaces, flows, wording, features. Distinct from how it looks in a feedback batch.

sections.title: Constitution & rules
sections.what: CLAUDE.md, docs/rulings.md, and the guard tests that enforce them. The amendment history — every rule added or changed, when, and which session changed it — is generated into docs/amendment-history.md by corepack pnpm rules:history, because it is derived from the commits rather than composed from memory.

sections.title: Repo & ops
sections.what: CI, tests, workflows, storage, the machinery the project runs on.
